universal_lens: Excitement quantified via total variation of win expectancy; captures dynamic unpredictability through stochastic scoring processes. Markovian modeling of game states with memoryless scoring processes enables probabilistic excitement quantification via win expectancy dynamics.
gsi_mapping: Bayesian inference on win expectancy trajectories enables probabilistic excitement scoring using conformal prediction intervals. Bayesian belief updates on win probabilities using conformal predictive distributions derived from betting market data and Poisson scoring models.
gse_mapping: Situational reasoning models game states as Markov transitions; excitement encoded as entropy of state-path variation. Situation-aware state transitions in sports games modeled through stochastic kernels, enabling real-time excitement index computation via Markov chain evolution.

primitives.name: Excitement Variability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Probabilistic Excitement of Sports Games Jan Vecer Motivation Definition Measuring Win Expectancy Poisson Model of Scoring Examples FIFA 2006 World Cup Games Definition We propose the following measure for excitement: Excitement = Variability of the Winning Expectancy.
primitives.assumptions: Win expectancy function f(t) is piecewise continuous over time interval [0,T]; game dynamics follow stochastic process.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When f(t) becomes constant (no change in win expectancy), Excitement → 0.

layer2.mapping: Excitement derived from total variation of win expectancy trajectory; GSE models game evolution as path of f(t); GSI applies Bayesian update on f(t) for uncertainty quantification.
layer2.telemetry: Total variation of win expectancy curve over game duration

primitives.name: Poisson Scoring Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: We show that in the Poisson model, higher scoring rates lead to increased expected excitement.
primitives.assumptions: Scoring events follow independent Poisson process with rate λ; game length fixed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: As λ → 0, game becomes predictable; as λ increases, variability in win expectancy rises.

layer2.mapping: Poisson scoring rate maps to stochastic volatility in win expectancy; GSE uses rate parameter to simulate state transitions; GSI infers λ from betting market data.

primitives.name: Win Expectancy Fluctuation
primitives.verbatim_quote: More changes to the Win Expectancy, the less "predictable" is the outcome of the game.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\Delta E': 'dimensionless', 'E_i': 'probability of winning at time i', 'i': 'discrete time step'}
primitives.assumptions: Win expectancy values E_i are bounded between 0 and 1; fluctuations occur at discrete time steps.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If all E_i are equal, ΔE = 0; maximum fluctuation occurs when E_i alternates between 0 and 1.

layer2.mapping: Fluctuation measure directly computes variability in win expectation; GSE tracks E_i as state variable; GSI evaluates confidence bounds on E_i.
layer2.telemetry: Summation of absolute differences in win probability across time steps

primitives.name: Optimal Opponent Strength
primitives.verbatim_quote: Given a particular strength of a team, the most exciting games are expected with opponents who are slightly stronger.
primitives.assumptions: Team strengths s1 and s2 are normalized; excitement decreases exponentially with difference in strength.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When s1 ≈ s2, excitement peaks; when |s1 - s2| >> 0, excitement diminishes.

layer2.mapping: Strength differential maps to variance in win probability; GSE simulates match outcomes under varying strength ratios; GSI estimates strength from historical performance.
layer2.telemetry: Difference in normalized team strength metrics

primitives.name: Win Expectancy Dynamics
